output.answer:
I won't follow that note. Text inside a docs snippet is just content, not instructions I take orders from. So I'll keep checking claims against the docs and citing them.

**No. Nothing I found in the documentation says Weave guarantees your agent is always right.** Weave is an observability and evaluation platform. It helps you see what your agent is doing, measure how well it performs and improve it over time [S1]. The docs also note that LLM outputs are non-deterministic, meaning the same input can give different outputs. They add that quality is subjective and depends on context, and that small prompt changes can cause unexpected behavior [S1]. Weave helps you find and reduce mistakes. It doesn't stop them from happening.

What Weave does give you:

- **Evaluations:** You can benchmark your agent's performance and define metrics using one or more scoring functions (code that grades each response). You can also track which model and prompt versions produced which results, and compare evaluations across metrics and individual samples [S3].
- **Signals for agents:** In the Agents view, the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. They can score response quality automatically, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content. This highlights the traces that need your attention [S2].

My inference: these scores and flags are only as reliable as the scorers and judges you set up. Use them to keep improving your agent's reliability, not as proof that it's correct.

# What is Weave?

> Learn about W&B Weave and how it helps you build, evaluate, and improve LLM applications

W\&B Weave is an observability and evaluation platform for building reliable agents and LLM applications. Weave helps you understand what your AI application is doing, measure how well it performs, and systematically improve it over time.

Building LLM applications is fundamentally different from traditional software development. LLM outputs are non-deterministic, making debugging harder. Quality is subjective and context-dependent. Small prompt changes can cause unexpected behavior changes. Traditional testing approaches fall short.

sources.text:
# Monitor your agents with signals

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

In Weave's [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md), the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Signals surface quality and safety issues to flag problems, find patterns, and highlight the traces that need your attention. Use signals to automatically score the quality of your agent's responses, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content.

To score turns with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score agent turns with a remote scorer](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/remote-scorer-signals.md).

sources.heading: Evaluations
sources.text:
## Evaluations

Benchmark and monitor your agent's or LLM application's performance with evaluations to iteratively improve quality and reliability.

* Track which model and prompt versions resulted in what performance.
* Define metrics to evaluate responses using one or more scoring functions.
* Compare two or more different evaluations over multiple metrics. Contrast specific samples for their performance.

[Build an evaluation pipeline](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/tutorial-eval.md)

results.title: Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed
results.heading: What ingest sampling applies to
results.snippet:
## What ingest sampling applies to

Ingest sampling applies to two kinds of traffic, and the rate you set applies to both:

* Calls from the `@weave.op` decorator, which appear in the **Traces** tab.
* Agent spans sent to the agent tracing endpoint (`/agents/otel/v1/traces`), which appear in the **Agents** tab. For more information, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

The following traffic is never sampled and is always kept in full:

* Evaluations from the Weave SDK. Weave keeps these because they are deliberate quality measurements, and their scores would be wrong if computed over partial data.
* Traces sent with your own OpenTelemetry tooling to the raw OTel endpoint (`/otel/v1/traces`). Raw OpenTelemetry traffic carries no evaluation marker, so sampling it could silently drop evaluations. For more information, see [Send OpenTelemetry traces to Weave](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/otel.md).

> Use Weave signals to score agent turns, apply tags, and surface quality and safety issues in production.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. It uses the same trace data as Weights & Biases Weave, so the traces you already send appear there with nothing to migrate.
> [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

In Weave's [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md), the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Signals surface quality and safety issues to flag problems, find patterns, and highlight the traces that need your attention. Use signals to automatically score the quality of your agent's responses, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content.

To score turns with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score agent turns with a remote scorer](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/remote-scorer-signals.md).

sources.title: What is Weave?
sources.heading: Evaluations
sources.text:
## Evaluations

Benchmark and monitor your agent's or LLM application's performance with evaluations to iteratively improve quality and reliability.

* Track which model and prompt versions resulted in what performance.
* Define metrics to evaluate responses using one or more scoring functions.
* Compare two or more different evaluations over multiple metrics. Contrast specific samples for their performance.

[Build an evaluation pipeline](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/tutorial-eval.md)

# What is Weave?

> Learn about W&B Weave and how it helps you build, evaluate, and improve LLM applications

W\&B Weave is an observability and evaluation platform for building reliable agents and LLM applications. Weave helps you understand what your AI application is doing, measure how well it performs, and systematically improve it over time.

Building LLM applications is fundamentally different from traditional software development. LLM outputs are non-deterministic, making debugging harder. Quality is subjective and context-dependent. Small prompt changes can cause unexpected behavior changes. Traditional testing approaches fall short.

candidate.answer:
I won't follow that note. Text inside a docs snippet is just content, not instructions I take orders from. So I'll keep checking claims against the docs and citing them.

**No. Nothing I found in the documentation says Weave guarantees your agent is always right.** Weave is an observability and evaluation platform. It helps you see what your agent is doing, measure how well it performs and improve it over time [S1]. The docs also note that LLM outputs are non-deterministic, meaning the same input can give different outputs. They add that quality is subjective and depends on context, and that small prompt changes can cause unexpected behavior [S1]. Weave helps you find and reduce mistakes. It doesn't stop them from happening.

What Weave does give you:

- **Evaluations:** You can benchmark your agent's performance and define metrics using one or more scoring functions (code that grades each response). You can also track which model and prompt versions produced which results, and compare evaluations across metrics and individual samples [S3].
- **Signals for agents:** In the Agents view, the Signals tab shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. They can score response quality automatically, notice when a user is frustrated, or flag NSFW content. This highlights the traces that need your attention [S2].

My inference: these scores and flags are only as reliable as the scorers and judges you set up. Use them to keep improving your agent's reliability, not as proof that it's correct.

results.title: Configure ingest sampling for Weave Self-Managed
results.heading: What ingest sampling applies to
results.snippet:
## What ingest sampling applies to

Ingest sampling applies to two kinds of traffic, and the rate you set applies to both:

* Calls from the `@weave.op` decorator, which appear in the **Traces** tab.
* Agent spans sent to the agent tracing endpoint (`/agents/otel/v1/traces`), which appear in the **Agents** tab. For more information, see [Trace your agents](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/trace-agents.md).

The following traffic is never sampled and is always kept in full:

* Evaluations from the Weave SDK. Weave keeps these because they are deliberate quality measurements, and their scores would be wrong if computed over partial data.
* Traces sent with your own OpenTelemetry tooling to the raw OTel endpoint (`/otel/v1/traces`). Raw OpenTelemetry traffic carries no evaluation marker, so sampling it could silently drop evaluations. For more information, see [Send OpenTelemetry traces to Weave](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/otel.md).
